newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end higher on foreign-led buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end higher on foreign-led buying.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended higher on Wednesday on foreign-led buying of big-caps as worries on the ongoing election campaign were seen subsiding, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index rose 7.24 points, or 1.10 percent, to close at a day high of 666.84 points.
Advancers led decliners by 61 to 58 with 71 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at around 438 billion rupiah.
"Foreign-led buying in Telkom and other big-caps was partly due to improved sentiment. Worries on the election campaign appear to be subsiding," one broker said.
Active Lippo shares included Lippo Securities which gained 125 rupiah to 1700 rupiah, Multipolar, up 100 rupiah to 1,725 rupiah and Lippo Life, up 100 rupiah to 3,050 rupiah.
Brokers said reports of the country's relatively healthy February trade surplus and a slight increase in the April consumer price index were likely to keep sentiment steady on big-caps.
Tin miner Timah fell 150 rupiah to 3,475 rupiah amid reports of lower first quarter net profit and the fact that the fabled Busang gold deposit was a dud, brokers said.
